- Avoid over-forecasting price spikes; model tends to overshoot after recent highs, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- Under-forecast downward moves in early periods; model often fails to anticipate sharp declines following recent peaks.
- When sentiment is consistently neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward overestimating short-term volatility and underestimating mean reversion.
- Correct for lagged reactions: model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends.
- Adjust forecasts downward if recent 3–5 day average is rising sharply and sentiment remains flat — model tends to ignore momentum.
- When true price exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 2–3% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00 and model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply downward correction of 3–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
